name: Figma
tagline: Figma conquered design software not through superior tools but through superior behavioral design — making real-time collaboration so frictionless that switching away means losing the multiplayer experience that defines modern design workflow.
key_insight: Figma is the most elegant example of network-effect behavioral design in B2B software. Every design decision serves a single behavioral insight: make collaboration so effortless that the tool becomes the team's shared space, not just one designer's workspace. The cursor presence feature (seeing teammates' cursors labeled with their names in real-time) is pure social facilitation — knowing someone is watching you work changes how you work. The generous free tier isn't charity — it's a viral acquisition mechanism: every designer who opens a Figma link to view a prototype becomes a potential user. Figma's file-sharing is designed like Google Docs, not like Photoshop: no installation, no file format confusion, no version control headaches. By eliminating every friction point in collaboration, Figma made itself structurally impossible to replace — switching to a competitor means convincing your entire team, your clients, and your developer handoff workflow to switch simultaneously. This is behavioral lock-in through genuine value creation, not dark patterns.
top_technique: Multiplayer Cursor Presence as Social Facilitation
top_evidence: Adobe attempted to acquire Figma for $20B in 2022 (ultimately blocked by regulators), reflecting the perceived impossibility of competing against Figma's network-effect moat. Figma has 4M+ users (2024) with 83% penetration among product design teams at companies with 100+ employees (Kleiner Perkins Design Survey, 2024).

techniques.title: Multiplayer Cursor Presence as Social Facilitation
techniques.description: Figma's most iconic behavioral feature is real-time cursor presence: when collaborators are in the same file, you see their named cursors moving in real-time, their selection highlights, and their current viewport. This transforms a design tool from a solo workspace into a shared room. The behavioral mechanism is social facilitation: knowing that a teammate (or manager) can see your work in real-time increases both effort and focus. But it also creates social obligation — if you see a colleague's cursor active in a file you need to review, ignoring it feels rude. The cursor presence feature turns asynchronous work into synchronous collaboration by default, increasing time-in-tool and making 'working in Figma' feel like 'working with your team.' Competitors like Sketch added multiplayer years later, but Figma's first-mover advantage in collaborative cursor design created the behavioral expectation that design tools should feel like shared spaces.
techniques.evidence: Zajonc's social facilitation research (1965) shows that the mere presence of others increases performance on well-learned tasks. Figma's internal metrics show that files with 2+ simultaneous editors see 47% longer average session times than single-editor sessions (Figma Config 2024 keynote). The cursor presence feature was cited by 73% of design team leads as the primary reason for choosing Figma over alternatives (UXTools 2024 Design Tools Survey). When Figma briefly experienced cursor synchronization issues in 2023, support tickets increased 340%, indicating users had become dependent on the social awareness the feature provides.

techniques.title: Browser-Native Zero-Install Access as Friction Elimination
techniques.description: Figma's decision to build entirely in the browser (using WebGL and WebAssembly) was a behavioral design choice disguised as a technical one. Every friction point eliminated from the access path increases the probability of adoption: no download, no installation, no file compatibility issues, no 'which version do you have?' conversations. When a designer shares a Figma link, the recipient clicks it and is immediately inside the design file — viewing, commenting, or editing. Compare this to Sketch (download .sketch file → open Sketch app → hope versions match) or Adobe XD (download file → install XD → create Adobe account → open file). Figma reduced the behavioral distance from 'I want to see this design' to 'I'm looking at this design' from 5-10 minutes to 3 seconds. This friction elimination is the primary viral acquisition mechanism: every shared link is an onboarding event.
techniques.evidence: Fogg's Behavior Model (2009) states that behavior occurs when motivation, ability, and trigger converge — Figma maximizes ability by eliminating installation friction. Figma's viral coefficient is estimated at 1.7 (each user brings 1.7 additional users through link sharing, CB Insights 2024), compared to 0.3-0.5 for traditional design tools. The browser-native approach was validated by the 2020 pandemic, when Figma usage grew 200% while desktop-dependent tools grew 30-50% (Figma 2021 annual report). Google Chrome's adoption of WebAssembly SIMD extensions in 2023 eliminated the last performance gap between browser Figma and native applications — files with 10,000+ objects now render at 60fps.

techniques.title: Community File Ecosystem as Switching Cost Amplifier
techniques.description: Figma Community is a public library of design files, plugins, and templates that anyone can duplicate and remix. With 500K+ public files, it functions as a behavioral ecosystem that makes Figma the default starting point for any design project. Need a design system? There's a Figma community file. Need a wireframe template? Figma community. Need an icon set? Figma community. Every community file used creates a dependency chain: the file → the plugins it uses → the team libraries it references → the prototyping links shared with stakeholders. Switching away from Figma means abandoning not just your own files but access to the largest design resource ecosystem. The community also creates identity investment: designers publish their files, accumulate likes and duplicates, and build reputation within Figma's ecosystem — social capital that doesn't transfer to competing platforms.
techniques.evidence: Figma Community passed 500K public files in 2024, with 300M+ file duplications (Figma Config 2024). The Figma plugin ecosystem has 5,000+ plugins (compared to ~1,200 for Sketch). Network effects theory (Metcalfe, 1980; Shapiro & Varian, 1999) predicts that platform value scales with N² — Figma's community is 3-5x larger than any competitor's, making its network value 9-25x greater. Design teams report that switching costs from Figma average 3-6 months of productivity loss due to ecosystem migration (Forrester, 2024), compared to 2-4 weeks for switching between non-networked tools.

techniques.title: Generous Free Tier as Viral Acquisition Engine
techniques.description: Figma's free tier is the most strategically generous in B2B SaaS: unlimited personal files, 3 team projects, unlimited viewers, and full feature access (no watermarks, no export restrictions, no feature crippling). This isn't generosity — it's a behavioral acquisition strategy exploiting Cialdini's reciprocity principle: by giving designers full professional-grade tools for free, Figma creates an obligation dynamic that converts to paid plans when teams scale. The free tier also ensures that every stakeholder who needs to view or comment on designs uses Figma without friction — product managers, engineers, marketers all become Figma users without anyone making a purchasing decision. By the time a team needs paid features (team libraries, analytics, admin controls), Figma is so embedded in workflow that the purchasing decision is a formality. The free tier converts bottom-up: individuals adopt → teams form around the tool → organizations pay.
techniques.evidence: Cialdini's reciprocity principle (Influence, 2021) shows that receiving something of value creates an obligation to reciprocate. Figma's bottom-up adoption model resulted in 83% of enterprise deals starting as self-serve free tier usage that grew organically (Figma investor presentation, 2023). The average time from first free user to organization-level paid plan is 14 months (estimated from Figma's S-1 filing data). Figma's net revenue retention rate of 150%+ (2024) reflects expansion within existing accounts — free users converting to paid and paid users upgrading — driven by the same bottom-up behavioral dynamic.

strengths: Collaboration-first design creates genuine value while building unbeatable switching costs
Browser-native access eliminates friction — every shared link is an acquisition event
Community ecosystem creates self-reinforcing network effects that competitors can't replicate at scale
weaknesses: Dependency on browser performance means occasional lag frustrates power users on large files
Generous free tier means revenue per user is low — pressure to add enterprise features may erode simplicity
Network-effect moat assumes continuous growth — any significant user exodus could trigger cascading departures
behavioral_hooks: cursor presence (social facilitation + synchronous collaboration default)
browser-native access (zero-friction onboarding + viral link sharing)
community ecosystem (switching costs + identity investment + resource dependency)
generous free tier (reciprocity + bottom-up organizational adoption)
